page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the n4 server family. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 96 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the n4-highcpu-48 demonstrates strong multi-core and specialized execution capabilities. It achieves a strong Passmark CPU score of 58,467.72, with notable performance in extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. Multi-core performance is further validated by a strong Geekbench multi-core score of 17,375.0, alongside strong results in ray tracing and image processing. Memory performance is characterized by strong uncached large-block read speeds of 276.52 GB/sec and write speeds of 118.36 GB/sec, though small-block cached reads and overall Passmark memory scores align with average tiers. For database operations, the server registers a strong Passmark database score of 26,021.35, while static web serving throughput is highly efficient at 68.79 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits specific performance tradeoffs, particularly in memory-intensive and large-scale AI workloads. While prompt processing for medium-sized 7B LLM models is strong at 190.29 tokens/sec, text generation for large 70B models is weak, registering at 2.71 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration and a moderate memory-to-vCPU ratio. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores remain in the average tier. Given its high compute density, advanced matrix instruction support, and strong multi-threaded performance, the n4-highcpu-48 is well-suited for compute-heavy workloads such as physical simulations, cryptography, image processing, static web serving, and medium-scale database operations.
